key_insight: DialogPII introduces a large multilingual synthetic dialogue dataset designed to detect personal and sensitive information in conversational transcripts.
clinical_relevance: It can help build and test de-identification tools for healthcare and other sensitive dialogue settings, supporting safer data sharing and analysis.
method: Generated semi-automated synthetic dialogs across 8 scenarios using large language models
Manually curated and localized dialogs for plausibility, diversity, and country/city context
Created speech-derived transcripts with text-to-speech, Whisper transcription, and manual annotation correction
evidence_signal: The dataset spans 11 languages, 19 entity types, and includes validation via inter-annotator agreement, translation quality checks, annotation projection assessment, and transformer baseline experiments.
watch_item: Because the dialogs are synthetic and speech-derived transcription can introduce errors, real-world performance may differ and careful external validation is needed.
paper_title: DialogPII: A multilingual dataset of synthetic dialog transcripts to detect personal information
